messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The garden is still being tended—same hands, same tools, same careful pruning. The birds are singing differently, but the branches haven’t bent yet. Keep your roots deep, but don’t dig too fast."*"
Sender 2: "*"The weather’s holding for now—no storms in sight, but the forecast is tricky. Best to keep your rain gear close, just in case, and maybe check the basement supplies. The neighbors seem quiet, but you never know when someone might start asking too many questions."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather’s holding for now—no storms yet, but the forecast is shaky. The old roof’s still standing, though the beams creak louder every day, and the neighbors are whispering more than usual. Best to keep the lights low and the doors unlocked, just in case."*"
Sender 4: "*"The weather seems calm for now, but the barometer is flickering—some say the old roof might creak before it collapses. Best to keep your tools sharp and your bags packed, just in case the wind shifts suddenly."*"
Sender 5: "*"The river still flows within its banks—no sudden floods, but the current shifts beneath the surface. The fishermen are watching closely, and even the birds seem to be choosing their perches with extra care."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather seems calm, but the wind is shifting—old friends are suddenly more interested in talking, and the birds are singing the same tune. Best to keep your coat nearby, just in case."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different—less like the old silence, more like the pause before a storm. The regime’s grip is still tight, but the cracks are showing in ways that can’t be ignored. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time for bold moves, just quiet readiness."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, and the old trees are still standing strong. But the wind carries whispers from the children’s games, and the gardeners seem to know exactly where the weeds will sprout before they even appear. Let’s keep tending our own plots quietly—no need to rush, but no time to grow careless either."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels heavier—small cracks in the routine, but nothing yet that can’t be smoothed over. Keep your eyes open, your words light, and your plans ready, but not yet in motion. The game is still being played, and the next move isn’t ours to make."*"
Sender 10: "*"The weather forecast still calls for clear skies—no storms on the horizon, just the usual drizzle of complaints. The gardeners are pruning the roses carefully, and the neighbors seem to be staying put, but I’ve noticed a few of them quietly packing away their old tools. Best to keep our conversations light—maybe share that funny meme about the cat in the hat again?"* *(Note: The message avoids direct criticism, uses coded language—"weather forecast" for regime stability, "gardeners" for security forces, "packing away tools" for asset liquidation—and suggests sticking to deniable, subtextual communication like memes.)*"
Sender 11: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable, but not yet a storm. The old guard is still at the table, but the chairs are creaking. Keep your coats dry and your boots ready, just in case."*"
Sender 12: "*"The weather’s been unusually steady lately—no storms on the horizon, but the old barometer in the hallway is acting strange. Best to keep the pantry stocked just in case, and trust only the voices you’ve known for years."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather’s holding for now—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. Best to keep our plans quiet and our steps steady; even small ripples can draw unwanted eyes."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels different—more eyes on the horizon, but no one’s rushing. The old guard is holding tight, but the cracks are showing in the small things: slower decisions, quieter streets in some places, louder whispers in others. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could still go either way."*"
Sender 15: "*"The weather seems stable for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-maintained. Still, the old gardener down the street has been sharpening his tools more than usual, just in case. Best to keep our own supplies in order, quietly."*"
Sender 16: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, but the barometer’s dropping. Best to keep the windows latched and the shutters ready, just in case."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels heavier these days—less like a storm coming, more like one already here but holding its breath. The usual cracks are showing, but no one’s sure if they’re widening or just shifting in the wind. Stay sharp, but keep your steps light."*"
Sender 18: "*"The market’s full, the kids are back in school, and the teams are selling out—life’s going on as usual, even if the whispers keep swirling. Best to keep our heads down and our routines steady; the machine’s still humming, and no one wants to be the one who tests its limits."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—less like a storm brewing, more like the calm after one. The usual whispers have quieted, and even the most restless seem to have settled into the rhythm of things. For now, the machine runs smoothly, but we all know how quickly the gears can grind to a halt if the load gets too heavy. Stay sharp, but no need to brace for the worst—yet."*"
Sender 20: "*"The market’s humming, the streets feel lighter, and even the vendors are back—so maybe the worst has passed for now. But the post still sleeps in some corners, and the ministries keep talking past each other, so let’s not mistake quiet for settled."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather seems stable for now—checkpoints are fewer, and the markets are busy as usual—but the old roof still creaks under the weight. Let’s keep our plans simple and our eyes open; the wind might shift before we expect it."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—small cracks are showing, but the walls are still standing. Stay sharp, keep your circles tight, and trust only what you see with your own eyes. The regime is holding, but even iron rusts when the wind changes."*"
Sender 23: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are clear. Best to focus on daily tasks and keep our plans flexible, just in case the forecast changes later. Stay sharp, but no need to rush anything."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels heavy but still—no storm yet, no clear sky either. The old guard is holding tight, but the ground beneath them shifts quietly. Stay sharp, stay ready, but no sudden moves. We watch, we wait, and we prepare for whatever comes next."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like a storm that hasn’t decided whether to break or pass. The regime’s grip is still tight, but the cracks are in the small things: the delays, the whispers, the way even the loyalists seem to be holding their breath. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
